passage: The corridor was crowded because rain kept everyone indoors, and children queued for the toilets. Vandana shoved a small boy out of the way and marched to the front. "I go first," she said, and her chest felt big and strong. Madhuri, the teacher, took her hand and stepped aside. "Pushing stops here. I won't let anyone be pushed." Vandana's chin wobbled. "My cousin does it," she muttered. Madhuri said gently, "You can be strong by being my line leader, holding the door." Vandana looked at her, then at the door, and slowly nodded.

qa.q: Why were the children crowded in the corridor?
qa.a: Rain kept everyone indoors, so children queued for the toilets.

qa.q: What was Vandana feeling when she pushed the small boy, and what might be under it?
qa.a: Vandana felt big and strong, but her wobbling chin suggests she may also feel sad or unsure. She says her cousin does it, so she may be copying someone.

qa.q: How did Madhuri set a firm limit and still stay warm?
qa.a: Madhuri said clearly that pushing stops and no one will be pushed. Then she offered another way to feel strong, as line leader holding the door.

qa.q: What might the small boy have felt when he was shoved?
qa.a: The small boy was probably startled and maybe frightened, since he was smaller. He would want a teacher to stop the pushing and keep the line fair.

grounding: A child pushes smaller children to feel powerful, and a teacher sets a firm limit warmly and offers another way to feel strong, without only punishing.

passage: At the village school, Irfan pushed the smaller boys off the tyre swing, one after another. He stood tall on it and laughed. When Bhavna Ma'am came, he was pushing little Chotu. "Irfan, stop. Pushing is not allowed." He sat out for ten minutes. Then she sat beside him on the bench. "You seem sad lately." Irfan kicked the dust. "Abba went to the city for work." "You miss him." Irfan nodded, his eyes wet. "Tomorrow, will you help me hold the swing for the little ones? Strong hands can help, too."

qa.q: What did Irfan push the smaller boys off?
qa.a: He pushed them off the tyre swing.

qa.q: What might Irfan be feeling underneath his pushing?
qa.a: He felt sad and was missing his Abba, who went to the city for work; pushing made him feel powerful for a moment.

qa.q: How did Bhavna Ma'am combine a limit with warmth?
qa.a: She stopped the pushing and gave him time out, then sat with him, noticed his sadness and offered him a way to be strong by helping.

qa.q: How might Chotu see Irfan holding the swing tomorrow?
qa.a: He may feel wary at first, then relieved to find Irfan helping instead of pushing.

grounding: A young boy who pushes smaller children is given a firm limit and a warm adult who notices his sadness and shows him another way to feel strong.

passage: In a kindergarten in Oslo, Ingrid kept pushing the smaller children out of the playhouse. "My house! Get out!" She looked strong and pleased. Clara, the teacher, stopped her. "Ingrid, no pushing. The playhouse is for everyone." Ingrid pushed again. Clara moved her gently to a bench. Then she sat beside her. "Where did you learn 'Get out'?" Ingrid shrugged. "My big brother says it. He pushes me off the sofa." Clara nodded. "Being strong can mean being the house captain who lets people in." At pick-up, Clara told Ingrid's father what she had said.

qa.q: What did Ingrid shout at the smaller children?
What might Ingrid feel underneath looking strong and pleased?
qa.a: She may feel small and pushed around herself, copying her big brother so she can feel powerful for once.

qa.q: Why did Clara do more than just punish Ingrid?
qa.a: Only punishing would not show her another way; Clara held the limit, asked where the words came from and offered a kinder way to feel strong.

qa.q: How might Ingrid's father feel after Clara talks to him at pick-up?
qa.a: He may be surprised and concerned, and want to help both his children play more gently at home.

grounding: A young girl pushes smaller children to feel powerful, copying her brother, and a teacher sets firm limits and teaches another way to feel strong.
